name: The Catcher in the Rye
kicker: J. D. Salinger’s 1951 novel · Teen alienation in one unforgettable voice
briefing: _The Catcher in the Rye_ follows sixteen-year-old Holden Caulfield during a restless few days in New York City after he is expelled from his prep school, Pencey Prep. J. D. Salinger tells the whole story in Holden’s own slangy, cynical voice as he dodges “phonies,” wanders the city alone, and aches for his little sister Phoebe and his dead younger brother Allie. The novel became one of the most read — and most banned — books in American schools.

qb.tip: All 9 giveaways end on Holden Caulfield’s name or “by J. D. Salinger” — Pencey Prep, Phoebe, and the ducks in Central Park are the most reused clues.

sample.note: the 9 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: One chapter of this novel reworks J. D. Salinger’s own earlier short story “Slight Rebellion Off Madison.” Its narrator tells the whole story while recovering someplace out West under a psychoanalyst’s care, and he flees his former English teacher Mr. Antolini’s apartment after waking to find the man patting his head.
tossups.r: That narrator also loses his fencing team’s equipment on a New York City subway car. For 10 points, name this novel narrated by Holden Caulfield.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator plays pinball with dormmates named Ackley and Brossard before getting into a fistfight with his roommate, Stradlater, over a girl named Jane Gallagher. Before that fight, he writes Stradlater’s English composition for him, describing a baseball glove covered in poems.
tossups.r: That glove belonged to the narrator’s late younger brother. For 10 points, name this novel in which Holden Caulfield is expelled from Pencey Prep.

tossups.p: At the Edmont Hotel, this novel’s narrator accepts the elevator operator Maurice’s five-dollar offer to send a young woman named Sunny to his room, though the awkward visit goes nowhere. Maurice later punches him in the stomach while Sunny takes extra money from his wallet.
tossups.r: The same narrator buys a red hunting cap in New York and wears it backward. For 10 points, name this novel about Holden Caulfield’s wandering weekend after leaving Pencey Prep.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator is shunned by his school’s fencing team after he leaves their foils and equipment behind on a subway car. He is also expelled from his Pennsylvania boarding school for failing four out of five classes.
tossups.r: He spends the following weekend wandering alone through New York City rather than go straight home. For 10 points, name this novel narrated by the teenager Holden Caulfield.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator resents his older brother D. B. for “selling out” as a screenwriter in Hollywood after once writing a short story the narrator admired. Throughout the book, that narrator constantly complains about “phonies,” people he sees as fake or hypocritical.
tossups.r: He misses his late younger brother Allie and dotes on his little sister Phoebe. For 10 points, name this novel by J. D. Salinger.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator visits his former English teacher, Mr. Antolini, late one night for advice, only to flee in alarm after the man pats his head while he sleeps on the couch. Confused and exhausted, the narrator spends the rest of that night on a bench in Grand Central Station.
tossups.r: Earlier that night, he had sneaked home to see his sister, Phoebe. For 10 points, name this novel whose narrator is expelled from Pencey Prep.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator repeatedly asks cab drivers where the ducks on a frozen Central Park lagoon go every winter. He also drops and breaks a rare record, “Little Shirley Beans,” that he bought as a gift for his little sister.
tossups.r: That sister, Phoebe, later talks him out of running away, and he watches her ride a carousel. For 10 points, name this novel starring Holden Caulfield.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator grows furious imagining his roommate Stradlater on a date with a girl named Jane Gallagher, whom he remembers fondly for the way she kept all her kings in the back row while playing checkers. The resulting fistfight leaves him with a bloody face.
tossups.r: He had already lost his school’s fencing equipment on the subway that same day. For 10 points, name this novel about Holden Caulfield’s expulsion from Pencey Prep.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator keeps a baseball glove covered in poems written in green ink by his brother Allie, who died of leukemia years earlier. He once broke his hand punching out the garage windows the night Allie died.
tossups.r: That narrator also treasures a record called “Little Shirley Beans” that he buys for his sister Phoebe. For 10 points, name this novel narrated by Holden Caulfield.

tossups.p: Near the end of this novel, its narrator sits in the rain outside a carousel, crying from happiness while watching his little sister reach for the gold ring as she rides. Earlier that day, he had planned to run away out West and live alone in a cabin.
tossups.r: He never fully explains to readers why he is telling this whole story from some kind of rest facility. For 10 points, name this novel narrated by Holden Caulfield.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator loves the Museum of Natural History specifically because its glass dioramas never change, unlike everything else in his life. He contrasts this permanence with his own confusion about growing up, which he associates with phoniness and loss.
tossups.r: He imagines a job standing in a field of grain, catching children before they tumble off a steep, unseen cliff nearby. For 10 points, name this novel about Holden Caulfield.

tossups.p: This novel opens at Pencey Prep, a Pennsylvania boarding school its narrator is about to leave for good after failing most of his classes. He first visits his elderly history teacher, Mr. Spencer, to say an awkward goodbye.
tossups.r: He then takes a train to New York City instead of going straight home to tell his parents. For 10 points, name this novel about Holden Caulfield’s expulsion.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator brags that his precocious little sister has gotten all A’s, joking that he is the only dumb one in the family. He also resents his older brother, D. B., a once-promising writer now working in the movie business.
tossups.r: That narrator secretly visits his sister’s school to leave her a note, since he plans to run away before she comes home. For 10 points, name this novel whose narrator is Holden Caulfield.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator addresses the reader directly from a rest home, where a psychoanalyst keeps asking whether he will apply himself at school. He refuses to tell his whole life story, starting instead from his last day at a Pennsylvania prep school.
tossups.r: Over the following rainy weekend, he wanders alone through New York City, calling nearly everyone he meets a phony. For 10 points, name this novel about Holden Caulfield.

tossups.p: The teenage narrator of this novel is expelled from yet another boarding school, Pencey Prep, just before Christmas break. Rather than go home immediately, he spends a lonely few days wandering around New York City.
tossups.r: He constantly complains about “phonies” and desperately misses his little sister, Phoebe, and his dead brother, Allie. For 10 points, name this novel by J. D. Salinger narrated by Holden Caulfield.

clues.t: Expelled from Pencey Prep, a Pennsylvania boarding school, at the very start of the novel
Deeply loves his practical little sister Phoebe, who talks him out of running away for good
Constantly complains that almost everyone he meets is a “phony”
J. D. Salinger’s only published novel, narrated entirely in its teenage hero’s own slangy voice
His younger brother Allie died of leukemia; he keeps Allie’s baseball glove, covered in poems
His roommate Stradlater fights with him after a date with a girl named Jane Gallagher
Keeps wondering where the ducks in Central Park’s frozen lagoon go every winter
Flees his former teacher Mr. Antolini’s apartment after the man pats his head while he sleeps
Resents his older brother D. B. for “selling out” to write movies in Hollywood
Hires a young woman named Sunny through the elevator man Maurice at the Edmont Hotel
Buys and wears a red hunting cap, often backward, throughout his wandering weekend
Tells the entire story from some kind of rest home, where a psychoanalyst is treating him
Breaks a rare record, “Little Shirley Beans,” that he bought for his sister Phoebe
Loses his school’s fencing team equipment on a New York City subway car
Reworks Salinger’s earlier short story “Slight Rebellion Off Madison” into one of its chapters
His siblings are D. B., Allie, and Phoebe Caulfield
Plays pinball with dormmates Ackley and Brossard shortly before his big fight with Stradlater
Says an awkward goodbye to his elderly history teacher, Mr. Spencer, before leaving Pencey
Loves the Museum of Natural History because its glass dioramas never change
Fondly recalls that Jane Gallagher always kept her kings in the back row while playing checkers
One of the most frequently banned books in American schools since its 1951 publication
Imagines a job catching children before they fall off a hidden cliff while playing in a field of grain

trap.title: The narrator, not the novel
trap.body: Holden Caulfield narrates this novel in the first person, and quiz bowl sometimes asks about him as a separate answer line. A clue describing “this character” or “this narrator” may want Holden Caulfield himself, while a clue asking you to “name this novel” wants the title, not the boy telling the story.
trap.fix: Listen for “novel” or “by J. D. Salinger” to know the title is wanted. If you’re tempted to blurt the author’s name instead of the title, hold off — Salinger wrote other books too, like _Franny and Zooey_.
trap.line: Real answer line: The Catcher in the Rye.
